topics.title: Meaning of Voice: Doer Focus vs Receiver Focus
topics.broadArea: Meaning of voice & Doer vs receiver focus
prerequisites: Clause elements S, V, O (Requires a short revision)

understand: Voice shows whether the grammatical Subject is the doer (Active) or the receiver (Passive) of the verb's action.
Shifting between Active and Passive changes focus/topic, not the real-world event or time.
identify: Classify sentences as Active Voice or Passive Voice by asking whether the Subject performs or receives the action.
construct: Pair an Active sentence with its matching Passive perspective for the same event.
commonMisconceptions: Thinking every Passive sentence describes the past because of -ed/-en verb forms.
Assuming the first noun (Subject) is always the doer of the action.

teachingProposal.shortExplanation: In Active Voice, the Subject does the action ('Mira waters the saplings'). In Passive Voice, the receiver moves into the Subject spotlight ('The saplings are watered by Mira'). The event stays the same—only the camera spotlight moves!

examples.text: Mira waters the mango saplings every morning.
examples.label: Active Voice (Doer Focus)
examples.note: Subject 'Mira' performs the action of watering.

examples.text: The mango saplings are watered by Mira every morning.
examples.label: Passive Voice (Receiver Focus)
examples.note: Subject 'The mango saplings' receives the action; time is still present habit.

commonMistakeToAddress.incorrectInterpretation: Thinking 'Fresh rice is grown in Odisha' is in Past Time because 'grown' is a past participle.
commonMistakeToAddress.correction: Look at the helper verb 'is': Present helper + Past Participle shows a regular present-time passive fact.

interactiveActivity.title: Who Is in the Subject Spotlight?
interactiveActivity.description: Students sort 6 school and nature sentences into 'Active (Subject = Doer)' and 'Passive (Subject = Receiver)' buckets.

checkpointQuestion.prompt: In 'Fresh guavas are packed in bamboo baskets every morning', what role does 'Fresh guavas' play?

options.label: The Subject and the doer packing the baskets
The Subject and the receiver of the packing action (Passive Voice)
An adverbial telling when the action happens
A past-time action completed yesterday

checkpointQuestion.explanation: 'Fresh guavas' is the grammatical Subject, but it receives the action ('are packed')—so the sentence is in Passive Voice.

topics.title: The Core Transformation Pattern (New Subject + be + Past Participle)
topics.broadArea: Subject/object movement & be + past participle structure
prerequisites: Past Participle V-en / V3 forms (Requires a short revision)

understand: Every Passive verb group contains two working parts: a form of 'be' (carrying tense and matching the new Subject) plus a Past Participle (V-en / V3).
Moving the Object into Subject position shifts Subject-Verb Agreement onto the new Subject.
identify: Locate the 'be' auxiliary and Past Participle inside a Passive sentence and verify new-Subject agreement.
construct: Convert simple Present and simple Past S+V+O sentences between Active and Passive Voice.
commonMisconceptions: Matching 'be' to the original doer instead of the new Subject ('The saplings is watered').
Dropping 'be' completely ('The kite flown by Arjun').
Using Simple Past V2 ('wrote', 'ate') instead of Past Participle V-en/V3 ('written', 'eaten').

teachingProposal.shortExplanation: Follow 4 clear moves: (1) Bring the Object to the Subject spot, (2) Add the matching form of 'be' for the time AND the new Subject, (3) Change the main verb to its Past Participle (V-en / V3), and (4) add 'by + original Subject' when helpful.

examples.text: Arjun wrote two science notes. -> Two science notes were written by Arjun.
examples.label: Singular-to-Plural Agreement + Irregular V-en
examples.note: New plural Subject 'Two science notes' requires 'were', and 'wrote' (V2) becomes 'written' (V-en/V3).

examples.text: The students clean the laboratory. -> The laboratory is cleaned by the students.
examples.label: Plural-to-Singular Agreement
examples.note: New singular Subject 'The laboratory' takes singular 'is', not 'are'.

commonMistakeToAddress.incorrectInterpretation: Writing 'The crisp dosas was served by our school canteen.'
commonMistakeToAddress.correction: The new Subject 'The crisp dosas' is plural, so 'be' must shift from 'was' to 'were'.

interactiveActivity.title: Build the Passive Transformation
interactiveActivity.description: Students rearrange colour-coded tiles (New Subject + matching 'be' + Past Participle + 'by' phrase) to convert an Active S+V+O sentence accurately.

checkpointQuestion.prompt: Which sentence correctly converts 'The gardener planted three neem saplings' into Passive Voice?

options.label: Three neem saplings was planted by the gardener.
Three neem saplings planted by the gardener.
Three neem saplings were planted by the gardener.
Three neem saplings are planted by the gardener.

checkpointQuestion.explanation: 'Three neem saplings' is plural and 'planted' is past time, so the verb needs plural past 'were' + Past Participle 'planted'.

topics.title: Voice Across Verb Tenses, Aspects & Modals
topics.broadArea: Verb form and auxiliary changes across tenses and modals
prerequisites: Tenses: Time and Verb Forms (Already available)
Modals structure bridge (Not yet available as standalone lesson)

understand: The original tense, aspect, or modal stays on the helping verb chain, while 'be / being / been + V-en' adds the passive layer.
Progressive passives require 'being'; Perfect passives require 'been'; Modals and 'will/going to' take bare 'be'.
Perfect Continuous and Future Continuous tenses do not have natural standard passive forms.
identify: Recognise whether a Passive verb chain expresses Simple, Progressive/Continuous, Perfect, Future-time, or Modal meaning.
construct: Transform Active sentences in Present/Past Simple, Present/Past Progressive, Present/Past Perfect, Future Time ('will', 'going to'), and Modals ('can, must, should') without shifting time.
commonMisconceptions: Dropping 'being' in ongoing passive actions ('The wall is painted right now' instead of 'is being painted').
Dropping 'been' in perfect passive actions ('The fruit has washed').
Changing Present Simple Active into Past Simple Passive.

teachingProposal.shortExplanation: Never change the sentence's time when changing Voice! Keep the tense or modal at the front of the verb chain, add the matching passive helper ('is/was', 'being' for -ing actions, 'been' for have/has/had, or 'be' after modals/will), and finish with the Past Participle.

examples.text: The students are painting a solar chart. -> A solar chart is being painted by the students.
examples.label: Present Progressive / Continuous Passive

examples.text: Mira has prepared fresh lemon water. -> Fresh lemon water has been prepared by Mira.
examples.label: Present Perfect Passive

examples.text: Everyone must follow library rules. -> Library rules must be followed by everyone.
examples.label: Modal Passive

commonMistakeToAddress.incorrectInterpretation: Converting 'Arjun is checking the rain gauge' into 'The rain gauge is checked by Arjun.'
commonMistakeToAddress.correction: 'is checking' means right now (ongoing). To preserve ongoing aspect, insert 'being': 'is being checked'.

interactiveActivity.title: Match the Tense-Aspect Passive Verb Chain
interactiveActivity.description: Students select the exact passive verb chain ('is being watered' vs 'is watered' vs 'has been watered' vs 'must be watered') to preserve the time clue in an Active sentence.

checkpointQuestion.prompt: Choose the accurate Passive version of 'ISRO has launched the weather satellite.'

options.label: The weather satellite was launched by ISRO.
The weather satellite has launched by ISRO.
The weather satellite has been launched by ISRO.
The weather satellite is being launched by ISRO.

checkpointQuestion.explanation: 'has launched' is Present Perfect; its passive keeps 'has' and adds 'been' before Past Participle 'launched'.

topics.title: Pronoun Case Swaps, Two Objects (SVOO), Questions & Imperatives
topics.broadArea: Pronoun changes, double objects, questions, and imperatives
prerequisites: Pronoun Case mini-bridge (Not yet available as standalone lesson)
SVOO, Interrogative, and Imperative patterns (Requires a short revision)

understand: Personal and interrogative pronouns change form between Subject and Object/by-phrase slots (I<->me, we<->us, he<->him, she<->her, they<->them, who<->whom).
Sentences with Indirect + Direct Objects (SVOO) can promote either Object to Subject (using 'to'/'for' before the retained Indirect Object).
Passive questions keep auxiliary-before-Subject inversion (replacing do/does/did with be); passive imperatives use 'Let + Object + be + V-en' or polite request frames.
identify: Spot accurate pronoun cases, valid dual SVOO passives, and inverted question word order.
construct: Convert sentences with pronouns, double objects, Yes/No or Wh- questions, and instructions into Passive Voice.
commonMisconceptions: Leaving Subject-case pronouns after 'by' ('by he', 'by they').
Leaving 'did/do/does' in a Passive question ('Did the chart drawn by Mira?').
Forgetting 'to'/'for' when promoting the Direct Object of an SVOO verb ('A glass of milk was handed Arjun').

teachingProposal.shortExplanation: When a pronoun crosses the verb, swap its case (I <-> me, she <-> her, they <-> them, who <-> whom). If a verb has two Objects ('gave Mira a medal'), either Object can lead! For questions, drop 'do/does/did' and place 'is/are/was/were' before the new Subject; for commands, use 'Let + Object + be + V-en'.

examples.text: She praised them. -> They were praised by her.
examples.label: Pronoun Case Swap

examples.text: The coach gave Mira a certificate. -> (A) Mira was given a certificate by the coach. / (B) A certificate was given to Mira by the coach.
examples.label: Two-Object (SVOO) Dual Passive
examples.note: Promoting the Indirect Object ('Mira') is most natural; promoting the Direct Object adds 'to'.

examples.text: Did the students clean the courtyard? -> Was the courtyard cleaned by the students?
examples.label: Yes/No Question Passive
examples.note: 'Did' is replaced by 'Was' placed before the new singular Subject 'the courtyard'.

examples.text: Water the saplings daily. -> Let the saplings be watered daily.
examples.label: Imperative Passive
examples.note: Uses 'Let + Object + be + V-en' for instructions.

commonMistakeToAddress.incorrectInterpretation: Converting 'Did Mira bring the globe?' into 'Did the globe brought by Mira?'
commonMistakeToAddress.correction: Passive questions never use 'do/does/did'; use past 'be' ('Was') before 'the globe' + Past Participle 'brought': 'Was the globe brought by Mira?'.

interactiveActivity.title: Swap Pronoun Cases & Question Openers
interactiveActivity.description: Students swap mismatched pronouns ('by they' -> 'by them') and replace 'Did' with 'Was/Were' to fix Passive questions and SVOO sentences.

checkpointQuestion.prompt: Which is the correct Passive form of 'Who planted this banyan tree?'

options.label: By who was this banyan tree planted?
By whom was this banyan tree planted?
Who this banyan tree was planted by?
By whom this banyan tree planted?

checkpointQuestion.explanation: After the preposition 'By', 'Who' changes to object form 'whom', and auxiliary 'was' precedes the Subject 'this banyan tree'.

topics.title: Using vs Omitting the 'by'-Phrase & Natural Passive Contexts
topics.broadArea: Use/omission of 'by' phrases & when passive is natural/useful

understand: The 'by + agent' phrase is omitted when the doer is unknown, obvious, or general ('someone, people, everybody, they').
Passive Voice is the natural grammatical choice in science processes, public notices, historical records, and result-focused writing.
Recognise 'by' (agent) vs 'with' (instrument/tool) or fixed state prepositions ('filled with', 'known to').
identify: Decide whether a 'by'-phrase is informative and necessary or redundant and better omitted.
construct: Rewrite vague-subject Active sentences ('Someone...', 'People...') into concise agentless Passive sentences.
commonMisconceptions: Mechanically adding '...by someone' or '...by people' to every Passive sentence.
Using 'by' before an inanimate tool ('cut by a knife' instead of 'cut with a knife').

teachingProposal.shortExplanation: Do not glue 'by...' onto every passive sentence! Drop 'by + doer' when the doer is unknown ('Someone left a scarf'), general ('People speak Odia here'), or obvious. Keep 'by + doer' only when naming the doer adds real meaning ('discovered by C.V. Raman'). Use 'with'—not 'by'—for tools ('sliced with a clean knife').

examples.text: Someone swept the library steps before dawn. -> The library steps were swept before dawn.
examples.label: Agent Omitted (Unknown Doer)
examples.note: 'by someone' adds zero information and sounds unnatural.

examples.text: The Konark Sun Temple was built in the thirteenth century.
examples.label: Natural Historical Passive
examples.note: Focuses smoothly on the heritage monument rather than a vague subject.

examples.text: The ripe mangoes were sliced with a clean steel knife by the cook.
examples.label: Tool ('with') vs Doer ('by')
examples.note: 'with' marks the instrument (knife); 'by' marks the human doer (cook).

commonMistakeToAddress.incorrectInterpretation: Converting 'People grow spices in Kerala' into 'Spices are grown in Kerala by people.'
commonMistakeToAddress.correction: 'by people' is redundant because only people cultivate crops. Write simply: 'Spices are grown in Kerala.'

interactiveActivity.title: Trim Unnecessary 'by'-Phrases & Fix Tool Prepositions
interactiveActivity.description: Students edit drafts with clunky '...by someone / ...by people' endings or '...by a spoon' tool errors into crisp natural Passive sentences.

checkpointQuestion.prompt: Which Passive sentence sounds most natural for 'Someone has returned the missing science book'?

options.label: The missing science book has been returned by someone.
The missing science book has returned.
The missing science book has been returned.
The missing science book was returned by people.

checkpointQuestion.explanation: Because the doer ('Someone') is unknown, omitting 'by someone' makes the Passive sentence natural while preserving 'has been returned'.

topics.title: Sentences That Cannot Be Made Passive (Intransitive & Linking Verbs)
topics.broadArea: Sentences that cannot be made passive
prerequisites: Clause patterns SV, SVA, SVC vs SVO (Requires a short revision)

understand: Only Transitive clauses containing an Object (SVO, SVOO, SVOC) can form a standard Passive sentence.
Intransitive clauses (SV, SVA) and Linking clauses (SVC) have no Object to move into Subject position.
Not every 'be + -ed' form is Passive: descriptive adjectives ('was excited', 'is closed') express a state rather than an action.
identify: Distinguish sentences that can become Passive from Intransitive, Linking, and state-verb sentences that cannot.
construct: Justify why an SVA or SVC sentence fails the 'Verb + what/whom?' Object test.
commonMisconceptions: Treating an Adverbial of place/time ('in the garden', 'at noon') as an Object.
Attempting to passivise linking verbs ('became', 'seems', 'looks') or state verbs ('resembles', 'belongs to').
Labelling 'The players were tired after practice' as Passive Voice.

teachingProposal.shortExplanation: Before converting any sentence, ask: 'Verb + what or whom?' If there is no Object—only a place/time phrase ('arrived at dawn', 'slept on the mat') or a Subject Complement ('is sweet', 'became captain')—there is nothing to move to the Subject spot, so NO Passive exists!

examples.text: The train arrived at six o'clock.
examples.label: Cannot Be Passive (Intransitive SVA)
examples.note: 'at six o'clock' tells when, not what the train 'arrived'.

examples.label: Cannot Be Passive (Linking SVC)
examples.note: 'sweet' describes 'The ripe mangoes', so there is no separate Object.

examples.text: The students were excited about the science fair.
examples.label: Not Passive (be + Adjective State)
examples.note: 'excited' describes how the students felt (compare 'very excited'), not an action done to them.

commonMistakeToAddress.incorrectInterpretation: Trying to convert 'Arjun sat on the wooden bench' into 'The wooden bench was sat on by Arjun' as a standard basic SVO passive.
commonMistakeToAddress.correction: 'sat' is intransitive and 'on the wooden bench' is an adverbial of place, not a Direct Object.

interactiveActivity.title: Passive-Possible or No-Object Trap?
interactiveActivity.description: Students sort 6 mixed sentences into 'Can Be Passive (Has Object)' vs 'Cannot Be Passive (No Object / Linking)'.

checkpointQuestion.prompt: Which sentence CANNOT be changed into Passive Voice?

options.label: The eco-club planted fifty bamboo saplings.
Warm sunlight filled the courtyard.
The morning breeze felt cool and fresh.
The teacher gave every runner a banana.

checkpointQuestion.explanation: 'felt' here is a linking verb followed by adjectives ('cool and fresh' describing the breeze). Without an Object, no Passive exists.

topics.title: Spotting and Fixing Common Voice Errors

understand: Most Active-Passive mistakes break one of five rules: Object availability, Pronoun case, 'be' tense/agreement match, Past Participle V-en form, or unnecessary 'by'-phrases.
identify: Pinpoint the exact structural error inside an incorrect Passive or Active transformation.
construct: Repair flawed Passive sentences cleanly so tense, aspect, agreement, participle form, and pronoun case all align.
commonMisconceptions: Fixing one part of a passive error (like 'was' -> 'were') while overlooking another ('wrote' -> 'written' or 'by he' -> 'by him').

teachingProposal.shortExplanation: Run every passive sentence through the 5-Point Voice Check: (1) Real Object? (2) Right pronoun case? (3) 'be' matches original tense AND new Subject? (4) Past Participle (V-en/V3) used? (5) Drop vague 'by someone/people'!

examples.text: Broken: 'The science posters was drew by they.' -> Fixed: 'The science posters were drawn by them.'
examples.label: 3-Fix Audit (Agreement + Participle + Pronoun)

examples.text: Broken: 'Did the broken chair repaired yesterday?' -> Fixed: 'Was the broken chair repaired yesterday?'
examples.label: Question Auxiliary Fix

commonMistakeToAddress.incorrectInterpretation: Writing 'A new library has built near our school.'
commonMistakeToAddress.correction: A library cannot build itself; insert 'been' between 'has' and 'built' -> 'A new library has been built near our school.'

interactiveActivity.title: 5-Point Voice Detective Audit
interactiveActivity.description: Students inspect flawed noticeboard and report sentences, diagnose which rule failed, and verify the repaired sentence.

checkpointQuestion.prompt: Find the error in: 'The fresh vegetables is being washed by she before lunch.'

options.label: Missing 'been' after 'is'
'is' should be 'are' (plural 'vegetables') and 'she' should be 'her'
'washed' should be 'wash'
The sentence cannot be passive because 'vegetables' is a noun

checkpointQuestion.explanation: Plural Subject 'The fresh vegetables' requires 'are being washed', and object position after 'by' requires 'her'.
